scope: Humidity-axis transcription product (task-humidity-axis): the OPAC 1998 free-troposphere composition and pinned WASO humidity-growth knots behind eclipse/aerosol.py's ft_growth_factor, with the preregistered interpolation semantics, layer-scope rulings and the R_RH verdict band consumed by validation/humidity_axis_inversion.py. Every value is a transcription or a mechanical derivation from pinned sources; no eclipse observation enters this product and no claim is made about whether humidity explains any event.
source_convention: quotes are verbatim text extracted from the pinned OPAC paper (sha256 below) via the task's extraction; locations give the printed page and the extraction file line anchors. The pinned PDF bytes are authoritative over the extraction text.

ft_composition.quote_sec5a_p842: The aerosol in the free troposphere is modeled by the continental components at a relative humidity of 50%, with a dominant part of the water-soluble component (n_i = 0.6 and m_i = 0.949), a certain part of soot (n_i = 0.4 and m_i = 0.0189), and some insoluble particles (n_i = 0.00017 and m_i = 0.032), which can be assumed for the Northern Hemisphere. A hypothetical number density of 730 particles cm-3 at sea level is assumed, allowing the use of (5d) for the description of height distributions, resulting, for example, in a number density of 390 particles cm-3 (M = 0.49 mg m-3) at a height of 5 km.

nongrowing_remainder_evidence.quote_sec4_p842: Mineral aerosol particles are assumed not to enlarge with increasing relative humidity.
nongrowing_remainder_evidence.dataset_structure: SOOT and INSO are pinned only as 00 files (no RH variants) in the sources.json enumeration of the 38 OPAC component files; the growth math carries their share as the RH-independent remainder q_rest (pinned by subtraction against the published 50%-RH total).
nongrowing_remainder_evidence.note: the subtraction avoids the unrecovered soot00/insoluble00 files; it is exact only under their RH-independence, which the dataset structure and the paper's construction support

table3_rh_semantics.quote_sec5a_p842: They are valid for a relative humidity of 80% in the case of the boundary aerosols and of 50% for the free troposphere.

ft_row.location: Table 3, printed p. 840-841 (extraction line 1991); the FT row is a background layer with no boundary-aerosol columns and no RH qualifier beyond the 50% reference stated in Sec 5a

stratosphere_row.comment: no RH state is declared for the stratospheric background row anywhere in the paper

table5_ft_row.location: Table 5 FT row (extraction line 2525): H_ft = 8 km

sec5b_upper_boundary.quote: For the proposed aerosol types, the upper boundary of this layer is always situated at 12 km.

repo_geometry_comparison.comparison: paper FT layer bounds (2-12 km) and scale height (8 km) equal the repository free-troposphere layer exactly (mechanical gate: tests/test_aerosol_humidity.py::test_ft_geometry_matches_repo_layer)
repo_geometry_comparison.profile_reference_note: the paper's FT profile references N(0)=730 particles/cm3 at sea level, N(z)=N(0)*exp(-z/8km); the repository layer is the bottom-referenced shifted exponential normalized to the same column AOD 0.013. The humidity growth enters as a column-AOD ratio f_FT(rh) = (E_waso(rh)+q_rest)/0.013 whose numerator and denominator share the same geometry and composition, so the ratio is invariant to the profile reference level; per-particle water uptake multiplies the extinction by the same factor at every altitude, so the repository's committed vertical shape is preserved and only the column AOD is rescaled (J1).

waso_growth_knots.extraction: ext.coef at 0.550 um from each pinned wasoNN file's optical table, per 1 particle/cm3 (row location recorded per knot in humidity_growth.json)
waso_growth_knots.missing_between_knots: the 80-98% WASO files are among the 12 unrecoverable component files (humidity_growth.json missing_rh_files); the 70-99% segment therefore carries the preregistered interpolation, and the sensitivity appendix of the A/B re-inversion records the log-RH alternative bracket

q_rest_derivation.formula: E_waso(rh) = n_waso * N(0) * e_waso(rh) * H * (exp(-bottom/H) - exp(-top/H)), with n_waso=0.6, N(0)=730 particles/cm3, e_waso the pinned ext550 knots, H=8 km, bottom=2 km, top=12 km; q_rest = 0.013 - E_waso(50%)
q_rest_derivation.gate: 0 < q_rest < 0.013 enforced at import of eclipse/aerosol.py (fail loud); pytest recomputes the chain from the pinned knots
q_rest_derivation.values_are: exact float results of the eclipse/aerosol.py implementation chain (the authoritative computation); pytest asserts identity

ft_growth_factor_pinned.definition: f_FT(rh) = (E_waso(rh) + q_rest)/0.013; monotone nondecreasing on the pinned domain

interpolation_semantics.rule: linear interpolation of the pinned per-particle ext550 knots in RH, then composition into the layer factor: f_FT(rh) = (E_waso(rh) + q_rest)/0.013
interpolation_semantics.outside_domain: fail loud (ValueError); the sub-reference direction is not implemented - no discriminator consumes it and the paper defines the FT composite reference state only at 50%

increment_layers.ruling: calibration-lane increment layers stay pinned at the 50% reference state (f=1): the (B-A) share measurement requires the humidity axis to be an attribute of the prior only, not of the calibrated increment - the same RH must not act twice through a calibrated artifact (J3)
increment_layers.antarctic_switch_rule: dormant (not triggered): the antarctic-type composition files (SUSO 6/8, SSAM 8/8, MITR 00 recovered) have pinned knots making synthesis feasible, and no increment layer consumes humidity under this ruling. Fallback chain preregistered for any follow-up task that humidifies increment layers: synthesize the antarctic composition first (Table 4 row, mass values at RH 50%: sulfate SUSO n_j=0.998, sea salt accumulation SSAM n_j=0.109e-2, mineral transported MITR n_j=0.123e-3; the SUSO 50% knot is missing and would need interpolation), switch to a WASO-class morphology only if synthesis proves infeasible

stratosphere_background.ruling: no humidity parameter: Table 3 declares RH states only for boundary aerosols (80%) and the free troposphere (50%), the stratosphere row carries none; the pinned SUSO data has no knots between 0 and 70% (50%/90% missing) so any low-RH stratospheric growth would need unpinned fabrication; stratospheric water vapor is decoupled from tropospheric event meteorology (J4)

r_rh_band.structural_domain: [1, infinity): R_RH is a max/min ratio of positive residuals; values below 1 are structurally unreachable and not preregistered
r_rh_band.band_edge_source: descriptive transcription of the mechanical edges imported from validation/extinction_gap_diagnosis.py (VERDICT_COMPATIBLE[1], VERDICT_TENSION[1]); the consumer asserts edge-value equality at import and applies the verdict through the imported constants only
r_rh_band.participation_rule: per ladder point: events with a positive inverted residual participate; zero-increment, over-closed and unclosed events are listed separately with their status; fewer than 2 participating events -> mechanical status degenerate, no band verdict
r_rh_band.evidence_grade_note: a ratio over n participating events is reported with n_participating; a 2-event ratio is not a 4-event R and carries weaker evidence
r_rh_band.interpretation_note: R_RH(70%) exceeding the raw R=7.110 is a necessary property of this closure semantics (the same absolute FT growth increment is removed from every event's baseline, so the residual ratio first widens and then narrows); it is neither a red flag nor evidence that humidity widens the spread
